encounters.cc: Sudden-onset left flank pain and gross hematuria in patient with recent nephrotic syndrome flare

lines: Sudden-onset left flank pain and gross hematuria in patient with recent nephrotic syndrome flare

The patient is an 8-year-old male with a history of relapsing minimal change disease (initially diagnosed July 2020, with recent relapse February 2022 following streptococcal pharyngitis) and obstructive sleep apnea who presents with sudden-onset left flank pain and gross hematuria.
He was diagnosed with minimal change disease three weeks ago after presenting with generalized edema and heavy proteinuria.
He was started on oral prednisone and initially responded well, with some reduction in swelling.
However, over the last two days, his parents report that he has seemed more fatigued and complained of vague abdominal discomfort.
This morning, he developed sharp pain in his left flank and passed dark red urine.
He denies dysuria, fever, or recent trauma.

lines: Facial puffiness and decreased urine output with tea-colored urine

This 11-year-old male with a history of relapsing minimal change disease previously complicated by renal vein thrombosis and prior streptococcal-related relapse is brought to the emergency department by his parents due to facial puffiness and decreased urine output for the past 2 days.
He had a mild fever and sore throat about 10 days ago that resolved without medical attention.
His mother noticed that his urine has become darker and appears “tea-colored.” He has been more fatigued than usual and refused to eat breakfast this morning.
